As of my last knowledge update in January 2023, Ghulam Ali Okarvi (also spelled as Kaukab Noorani Okarvi) is a Pakistani Islamic scholar and preacher associated with the Sunni Barelvi movement. Born in 1957 in Karachi, Pakistan, he is known for his strong adherence to the teachings of the Ahl-e-Sunnat Wal Jamaat (the mainstream and orthodox Sunni tradition within the Indian subcontinent) which also significantly aligns with Sufi beliefs and practices.

He is the son of Muhammad Shafee Okarvi, a prominent religious scholar, who was also esteemed in the Barelvi movement. This lineage has contributed to Ghulam Ali’s standing and authority within the community.

Ghulam Ali Okarvi has authored numerous books and delivers sermons focused on Islamic theology, jurisprudence, the life of the Prophet Muhammad, and the virtues of the Sahaba (the companions of the Prophet). His speeches often emphasize love and respect for the Prophet Muhammad and include significant discussion on the importance of following the Sufi traditions and practices. He has also extensively spoken against beliefs and practices that differ from his own interpretations of Sunni orthodoxy, often engaging in debates and arguments with theologians from other Islamic schools of thought.

Okarvi’s influence extends beyond the borders of Pakistan, seen in his participation in numerous international conferences and gatherings. He has a notable presence across various media platforms where his lectures on Islamic topics reach a broader audience. However, like many religious figures, his viewpoints can be polarizing and are sometimes criticized by those who adhere to different Islamic interpretations or more secular viewpoints.

His significant contributions also include working on religious educational projects, participating in charitable activities, and promoting a version of Islam that he believes aligns closely with compassion, peace, and spiritual devotion.
